questions.title: In BitNet b1.58, is the ternary weight matrix rescaled by $\gamma$ after matmul, or is the scale dropped?
questions.question_body: In "The Era of 1-bit LLMs: All Large Language Models are in 1.58 Bits", the ternary weights are obtained via $\tilde{W} = \mathrm{RoundClip}(W/(\gamma+\epsilon), -1, 1)$ with $\gamma = \frac{1}{nm}\sum_{ij} |W_{ij}|$. In many ternary schemes one uses $W_q \approx \gamma \cdot \tilde{W}$ and applies a scalar rescale after the matmul. Here it is unclear whether inference uses only $\tilde{W}$, or whether there is a dequantization multiply by $\gamma$ (per-tensor or per-channel) on the output. If there is a rescale, where does it happen and is that multiply counted in the latency/energy results? If there is no rescale, how is magnitude information recovered elsewhere?

questions.title: What does "1.58 bits" mean in practice if the kernel packs weights in 2 bits?
questions.question_body: The paper calls the model "1.58-bit" because weights are ternary $\{-1,0,1\}$ (entropy $\log_2 3 \approx 1.585$), but the implementation uses the Ladder 2-bit kernel. Are the reported memory/latency results based on 2-bit physical packing, or do you use any entropy coding to approach 1.58 bits/weight? How are per-tensor scales, padding/alignment, and metadata counted in memory totals? When should we think in terms of 1.58 bits vs 2 bits for practical deployments?

questions.title: Over which axis is the absmean scale $\gamma$ computed, and why not per-channel or groupwise scaling?
questions.question_body: You define $\gamma = \frac{1}{nm}\sum_{ij}|W_{ij}|$, i.e., an abs-mean over the entire matrix. Many quantization methods use per-output-channel (row-wise or column-wise) or groupwise scales to improve fidelity. Why choose a per-matrix abs-mean here? Did you try per-channel $\gamma_c = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |W_{ic}|$ or groupwise variants, and what were the accuracy/speed trade-offs? Does per-channel scaling add too many post-matmul multiplies that hurt the "almost no multiplication" claim?

questions.title: How are gradients passed through the non-differentiable RoundClip—do you use an STE, and with what details?
questions.question_body: During training, $\tilde{W} = \mathrm{RoundClip}(\cdot)$ is piecewise constant. Do you use a straight-through estimator with $\partial \tilde{W}/\partial W = 1$ in some range and $0$ outside, or another surrogate? How are gradients handled at the clip boundaries $\pm 1$? Is there any gradient scaling/annealing on $W/(\gamma+\epsilon)$ early in training to control quantization noise?

questions.title: Per-token activation quantization to $[-Q_b, Q_b]$: what exactly is "per token", and how are scales computed and applied?
questions.question_body: The paper states that activations are 8-bit, scaled to $[-Q_b,Q_b]$ per token, and the zero-point is removed. Does "per token" mean per batch element and sequence position independently, over the hidden dimension of each layer? Is the scale $s$ computed as $s = Q_b/\max(|x|)$ or via an abs-mean/percentile? Is $Q_b=127$ (symmetric int8)? Are scales recomputed at every layer and time step in decoding, and what is the runtime overhead of this dynamic scaling?

questions.title: Does per-token scaling disturb attention calibration? How are $QK^\top$ dot products handled with different scales per token?
questions.question_body: If each token's hidden vector is quantized with its own symmetric scale, queries $Q$ and keys $K$ may have token-dependent scales. Before computing $QK^\top$ and softmax, do you dequantize to a common floating-point domain, or carry per-token scales into the dot product and renormalize analytically? Any observed impact on attention score variance or the effective softmax temperature due to per-token quantization?

questions.title: How is SwiGLU implemented with 8-bit activations—do you dequantize around SiLU or keep everything integer?
questions.question_body: In LLaMA-like MLPs, SwiGLU applies two linear projections followed by a SiLU gate and elementwise multiplication. With int8 activations, are the tensors entering SiLU upcast to FP16/BF16 for the nonlinear and then requantized, or are these kept purely in integer arithmetic? Did you observe any accuracy degradation specific to the SwiGLU gate under symmetric int8 activation quantization?

questions.title: How does the Ladder 2-bit kernel implement ternary-weight matmuls with int8 activations—adds/subs only, or bit-serial tricks?
questions.question_body: With weights in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and int8 activations, a straightforward approach would use add, subtract, or skip per weight. On GPUs, that could be branchy or bandwidth-bound. How does the Ladder 2-bit kernel realize this efficiently in practice? Do you encode ternary values as two binary masks (nonzero and sign) and fuse them with vectorized additions, or use popcount/XNOR-like techniques adapted from binary networks?

questions.title: 71.4x arithmetic energy savings claim: what op-energy constants, accumulator width, and memory costs were assumed?
questions.question_body: You report that on 7 nm, BitNet b1.58 saves 71.4x arithmetic energy for matrix multiplications versus FP16. Can you list the per-op energy numbers used (e.g., FP16 multiply, FP16 add, int8 add, int32 accumulate), the assumed accumulator precision, and the operation mix per MAC? Was memory energy (reads/writes from SRAM/DRAM) included, or is 71.4x compute-only? A worked example for a representative GEMM shape would be very helpful.

questions.title: KV cache precision and "lossless compression to 4 bits": is the cache currently 8-bit, and what does "lossless" mean?
questions.question_body: The paper claims 8-bit activations reduce KV cache size and that it can be "losslessly compressed" to 4 bits or lower. Are $K$ and $V$ currently stored as int8 during decoding? By "lossless to 4 bits", do you mean entropy coding that preserves exact int8 values, or an additional quantization that shows negligible accuracy loss (i.e., not truly lossless)? If entropy coding is intended, what compression ratios and runtime overheads do you observe?

questions.title: Why does parity with FP16 emerge only around 3B parameters—what breaks at smaller scales?
questions.question_body: Results suggest BitNet b1.58 starts to match FP16 LLaMA around 3B parameters. For 1B or smaller, is the gap driven by representational limits of ternary weights, optimization challenges (e.g., gradient noise with heavy quantization), or architecture hyperparameters tuned for FP16? Any ablations that vary width vs depth at fixed parameter count, or adjust MLP expansion/attention head counts, to isolate the capacity most affected by ternary constraints?

questions.title: How much ternary-induced sparsity do you observe, and is it exploited for speed on current GPUs?
questions.question_body: Allowing $0$ in $\{-1,0,1\}$ should induce weight sparsity. What fraction of weights are zero per layer at convergence (mean, variance across layers), and how does this differ between attention and MLP blocks? Does your kernel actually skip arithmetic for zeros to gain speedups, or are current GPU paths effectively dense so sparsity only helps conceptually (e.g., for future hardware)?

questions.title: Why compare mainly to FP16 rather than strong 3–4 bit quantized baselines (e.g., AWQ, GPTQ)?
questions.question_body: Given that 4-bit post-training quantization with int8 activations is widely used, it would be informative to compare BitNet b1.58 to well-tuned 3–4 bit PTQ/QAT baselines on both accuracy and decode-time latency/memory. Do your Pareto gains hold against these baselines, especially at 3B–13B scales?

questions.title: Decode-time latency measurement details: prompt length, batch size, hardware/software stack, and prefill vs decode split?
questions.question_body: You report "time per output token" using FasterTransformer with the Ladder 2-bit kernel. To reproduce, could you specify: GPU model and memory (e.g., A100 80 GB), CUDA/cuBLAS/cuDNN versions, prompt length for prefill, batch size(s), sequence length, attention implementation (e.g., paged KV cache), and whether you report pure decode latency or an average over prefill+decode? Was the FP16 baseline using fused attention/FlashAttention and any autotuning comparable to the ternary kernel?

questions.title: During training, are FP32 "master" weights kept and quantized on-the-fly, or are parameters stored strictly as ternary?
questions.question_body: For quantization-aware training, it is common to maintain high-precision "master" weights and apply $\tilde{W}$ only in the forward pass via an STE. Did you keep FP32/BF16 master weights and optimizer states, or were parameters constrained to ternary at all times? What was the training-time memory footprint and throughput relative to an FP16 LLaMA trained with the same tokens?

questions.title: Is $\gamma$ recomputed each forward pass per matrix, and how sensitive is training to $\epsilon$ or to using a moving average?
questions.question_body: In $\tilde{W}=\mathrm{RoundClip}(W/(\gamma+\epsilon),-1,1)$ with $\gamma=\text{absmean}(W)$, do you recompute $\gamma$ from the current real-valued $W$ each step, or maintain an EMA across steps to stabilize scaling? What value do you use for $\epsilon$, and how sensitive are results to it? Did you try median/percentile-based scales to reduce outlier effects?

questions.title: What accumulator precision is used for the int8-by-ternary dot products, and how do you prevent overflow?
questions.question_body: With int8 activations in $[-127,127]$ and weights in $\{-1,0,1\}$, the worst-case dot product magnitude is $127d$ for length $d$. For typical widths (e.g., $d=8192$), this fits in int32 but not int16. Do your kernels accumulate in int32 and then rescale, and are there any intermediate downscales or blocking strategies to guard against overflow in very wide layers?

questions.title: What drives the larger speedups at bigger model sizes—compute-bound vs memory-bound effects?
questions.question_body: You report that speedup increases with model size (e.g., 4.1x at 70B). Is this mainly because a larger fraction of time is spent in BitLinear GEMMs as depth/width grow (shifting to compute-bound where int8 adds excel), or because bandwidth pressure is reduced by smaller weights? Do you have a roofline-style analysis contrasting FP16 vs ternary across sizes to illustrate the regime shift?

questions.title: Can you formalize the claimed "new scaling law"—a function relating quality and cost for 1.58-bit vs FP16?
questions.question_body: Beyond the qualitative equivalences (e.g., 13B 1.58-bit is more efficient than 3B FP16), can you provide fitted relationships such as $\text{PPL}(N,T,b)$ vs parameter count $N$, training tokens $T$, and bit-width $b$, and a cost model $C(N,b)$ for latency/memory/energy? This would enable plotting iso-quality iso-cost curves to plan model sizing. How robust are these fits across datasets and modest architecture variations?

questions.title: What exactly is counted in the reported GPU memory numbers—weights only, or also KV cache and temporary activations?
questions.question_body: For the runtime memory comparisons, do the numbers include: quantized weights (plus any per-tensor scales), KV caches at the stated batch size and context length, intermediate activations during prefill, and workspace buffers from FasterTransformer? Are optimizer states excluded (inference-only), and were the measurements taken at batch size 1 decode or at the maximum batch that fits?
